newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia seen trebling uranium exports-ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia seen trebling uranium exports-ABARE.

text.p: Australia could treble its uranium exports to a value of more than A$800 million a year early in the next decade following the ending of Australia's three-mine uranium policy, a senior official of the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Monday.

Australia could feasibly export as much as 17,000 tonnes of uranium oxide (U308) by early next decade, Tom Waring, manager minerals energy and resources at ABARE, told a uranium conference. This could yield export revenue of A$828 million in 1996/97 terms, up from A$242 million in 1995/96, he said.
The 1995/96 exports were drawn from Australia's two operating mines, Energy Resources of Australia Ltd's Ranger mine in the Northern Territory and WMC Ltd's Olympic Dam mine in South Australia.

The third mine in Australia's three mine uranium policy, enforced by the former Labor government but abolished in 1996 by the present Liberal-National government, was Nabarlek in the Northern Territory which ceased production in 1988.
In 1995/96, ERA exported 3,454 tonnes of U308 from Ranger, while WMC exported 1,653 tonnes from Olympic Dam.
New production from Australia is expected to contribute significantly to expanding world requirements of new mine production, Waring said.
He forecast that several new Australian uranium mines would come into production in the medium term.

ERA's Jabiluka mine, north of the existing Ranger mine in the Northern Territory Kakadu National Park is planned to open in 1999, while the RTZ-CRA Kintyre deposit is expected to be brought into production the same year, he said.
The Beverley deposit in South Australia, owned by a subsidiary of General Atomics Corp of the United States, is expected to begin production in year 2000, he said.
Waring said the Cogema Australia-owned Koongarra deposit in Kakadu National Park was not expected to be exploited in the medium term but could go ahead early next decade.
MIM Holdings Ltd's Honeymoon deposit in South Australia is not expected to be exploited in the medium term, nor is WMC's Yeelirrie deposit in Western Australia, he said.
Other deposits not expected to be mined in the medium term are RTZ-CRA's Westmoreland in Queensland, Cogema's Ben Lomond in Queensland and Cogema's Manyingee in Western Australia.
